summary: Bhagavan Das was an Indologist and philosopher who earned an M.A. from the University of Calcutta. He served as Honorary Secretary at Central Hindu College (~1899–1914) and headmaster of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (~1921–1940).
Bhagirath Prasad Tripathi is an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1976), where he later served as head of the Research Department (attested 1989).

Bhagwan Dash worked in Indology and Tibetology, studying at the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda, Tribhuvan University, and the University of Delhi (Ph.D. 1978). He served as a bibliographer and cataloguer at the Library of Congress.

Bhagwanlal Indraji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who received an honorary doctorate from Leiden University in 1884. He was a member of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (~1877–1888) and a Fellow at the University of Mumbai (1882).

Bhajagobinda Ghosh worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 1994, he was attested as an Editorial Board Member of the Bulletin of Tibetology and Assistant Director at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Bharat Bhushan Vidyalankar is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Gurukula Kangri Vishwavidyalaya, the University of Delhi, and Dr. Bhimrao Ambedkar University. He held posts at Kendriya Hindi Sansthan and Sandhaan (1991).

Bhau Daji was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He completed his education at Elphinstone College (~1840–1843) and Grant Medical College and Sir Jamshedjee Jeejeebhoy Group of Hospitals (~1845–1850).
Bhesh Narayan Dahal works in Indology and history and archaeology. In 2018, he was attested at the National Archives of Nepal and served on the editorial board of Documenta Nepalica.

Bhikkhu Anālayo works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Ceylon and completing his Habilitation at the University of Marburg. His posts include positions at the University of Hamburg and the Barre Center for Buddhist Studies.

Bhikkhu Bodhi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from Claremont Graduate University. He served as editor at the Buddhist Publication Society (1984–2002) and president of the Buddhist Association of the United States (2013).

Bhikkhu Pāsādika works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, earning a Ph.D. from Punjabi University. He held teaching posts at Punjabi University (1975–1977) and the University of Marburg (1995–2007), and was president of Linh Son Buddhist Academy (2016).
Bhikkhu U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts degree at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under the supervision of Sanu Mahatthanadull (attested 2017).

Bhikkhuni Dhammanandā works in Buddhist studies. She earned her Doctor of Philosophy at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007), supervised by Tilak Kariyawasam and Daya Edirisinghe.

Bhogilal Sandesara was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Rasiklal Chhotalal Parikh. He served as Head of the Gujarati Department at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda (~1951–1975) and Director of the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (~1958–1975).

Bhuwan Lal Joshi was an Indologist educated at Patna University. He held academic posts at the University of California, Berkeley (~1960–1965) and served as a professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz (~1965–1977).

Bidia Dandaron was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1934–1937) under Andrei Vostrikov. In 1957, he served as a research fellow at the Institute of Mongolian, Buddhist and Tibetan Studies.

Bihani Sarkar works in Indology and religious studies. She held a post at the University of Hamburg and serves as Senior Lecturer in Comparative Non-Western Thought at Lancaster University (attested 2026).
Bill M. Mak held a post at Kyoto University (attested 2017) and is attested as a Research Fellow at the University of Hamburg in 2026.

Bimal Krishna Matilal was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard under W. V. O. Quine. He was a professor at the University of Toronto (~1968–1976) and Spalding Professor at the University of Oxford (1977–1991).

Bindeshwari Prasad Sinha was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at the University of London under Lionel David Barnett. He served as head of department at Patna University (1958) and Honorary Joint Director of K. P. Jayaswal Research Institute (~1969–1977).
